site.name: Physics Playground
site.tagline: Physics experiments you can play with right in your browser.
site.description: Interactive physics simulations for students: free fall, a spring launcher, a draining bucket, an electric field and a car you drive. Nothing to install.

home.heroText: Pick an experiment, change anything you like and see what happens. On Earth, on Mars or on the Moon.
home.heroCanvasLabel: A ball falls to the ground. The faint circles show where the ball was every quarter of a second.

sim.comingSoonText: We're moving it from Python to the website. Until then, you can see the original version on GitHub.

free-fall.title: Free fall
free-fall.blurb: A heavy object and a light one are dropped together. Which lands first?

spring-launcher.title: Spring launcher
spring-launcher.blurb: Squeeze the spring, pick an angle and launch the ball. How far does it go?

bucket.title: Draining bucket
bucket.blurb: Water pours out through a hole. Why is it fast at first and slow at the end?

electric-field.title: Electric field
electric-field.blurb: Electric charges pull and push. Follow a particle as it moves between them.

car.title: At the wheel
car.blurb: Press the pedals and drive. How do distance, speed and acceleration change?

freeFall.airNoteEarth: Earth's air at sea level: 1.225 kg/m³.
freeFall.airNoteMoon: The Moon has no air, so this changes nothing.
freeFall.airWarning: Air is on, so the formula is no longer exact.
freeFall.resultAlmost: Same to 1/100 s: the air here is thin.
freeFall.noteReady: Press Drop to draw the graphs.
freeFall.noteNoAtmosphere: No atmosphere here, so the air switch changes nothing.
freeFall.noteAir: Air on: the lighter ball levels off at its top speed.
freeFall.noteLanded: Both lines are exactly on top of each other.
freeFall.noteFalling: Watch one line: the other is hidden underneath it.
freeFall.sceneLabel: Two balls dropped side by side from {h} m.
freeFall.whatText: Earth pulls harder on the heavy ball, but the heavy ball is also harder to get moving. The two effects cancel exactly, so without air everything falls at the same rate: t = √(2h/g). There's no mass in that formula!
freeFall.shortcutsText: Space: drop / pause · R: reset · A: air · 1/2/3: world · + / −: speed

quiz.title: Quiz
quiz.question: Question {n} of {total}
quiz.scorePerfect: Perfect! You're ready for the bonus questions.
quiz.scoreGood: Well done! Read the explanations again for the ones you missed.
quiz.scoreLow: No problem: play with the simulation, then try the quiz again.
quiz.bonusIntro: These have no options to pick from. Think, talk it over with someone, then check the answer.
quiz.intro: {total} questions. Pick an answer and press Check.

spring.landed: Landed {d} m away after {t} s, exactly as the formula predicted!
spring.ready: The ball is sitting on the squeezed spring. Press Launch!
spring.noteReady: Press Launch! to draw the graphs.
spring.noteEnergy: The red (total) line is flat: energy is never lost, it just swaps between motion and height.
spring.noteVelocity: vx stays the same the whole flight; only vy changes: it goes up, reaches zero at the top, then down.
spring.sceneLabel: A spring launcher fires a ball at {a}°.
spring.whatText: A squeezed spring stores energy: E = ½·k·x². Let go, and all of it becomes the ball's motion: ½·m·v² = E. In the air, gravity only changes the up-and-down speed; the sideways speed stays the same. The total energy stays the same all the time: it just moves between motion and height.
spring.shortcutsText: Space: launch / pause · R: reset · V: speed arrows · 1/2/3: world · + / −: speed

bucket.ready: The hole has a plug in it. Press Pull the plug!
bucket.emptyAfter: Empty after {t}. The first half of the water took {a}, the second half {b}: {r} times slower!
bucket.noteReady: Pull the plug to draw the graphs.
bucket.noteRun: The height falls fast at first, then slower and slower. The jet speed falls in a straight line: v = √(2gh).
bucket.sceneLabel: A bucket with {v} litres of water and a {d} mm hole near the bottom.
bucket.whatText: Water leaves the hole at v = √(2gh), where h is the height of water above the hole (Torricelli's law). More water pushes harder, so the jet is faster. As the bucket empties, h drops and the jet slows down. That's why the second half of the water takes much longer than the first.
bucket.shortcutsText: Space: pull the plug / pause · R: reset · 1/2/3: world · + / −: speed

field.full: That's {n} charges, the most that fit.
field.selectedHint: The selected charge also moves with the arrow keys.
field.noSelection: Tap a charge to select it.
field.hint: Tap anywhere to put the particle there. Drag the charges to move them.
field.energyNote: The total energy stays the same: it just moves between motion and the field.
field.zeroForce: The force is exactly zero here: the pushes cancel out.
field.stopHit: The particle hit a charge and stopped.
field.noteReady: Release the particle to draw the graph.
field.sceneLabel: An electric field with {n} fixed charges and a test particle.
field.whatText: Each fixed charge pushes or pulls the particle: like charges repel, opposite charges attract. The force drops fast with distance: at twice the distance it's 4 times weaker (F = k·q₁·q₂/r²). The red arrows show which way a positive charge would be pushed at each point, and the yellow arrow shows the force on the particle.
field.shortcutsText: Space: release / pause · R: reset · F: field arrows · Delete: remove the selected charge · + / −: speed

car.pedalHint: Press and hold a pedal. Lower down = harder.
car.freeText: Green pedal: speed up. Red pedal: slow down. Watch the distance markers, the graphs and the fuzzy dice.
car.noFriction: This road is perfectly smooth, like ice, and there's no air: nothing slows the car down except the brake.
car.cruiseStep3: Watch the speed for {s} seconds. What happens?
car.cruiseDone: The speed stayed at {v} m/s the whole time! Nothing pushes back on this road, so the car just keeps going. That's Newton's first law. The dice hung straight too: at a steady speed there is no acceleration.
car.cruiseStopped: The car stopped. Press the gas to get going again.
car.parkText: Stop with the front of the car right on the yellow line at {d} m. Speed up, then brake at the right moment!
car.parkPerfect: Only {d} m from the line. Perfect parking!
car.parkShort: You stopped {d} m before the line.
car.parkLong: You stopped {d} m past the line.
car.parkTip: Tip: braking distance grows fast with speed. Twice as fast needs four times as far to stop.
car.parkBest: Your best this time: {d} m from the line.
car.eqSpeedQ: Speed: how many metres in one second?
car.eqAccelQ: Acceleration: how much faster in one second?
car.eqWaiting: Drive for a moment to see the numbers.
car.eqMore: For the curious: make Δt smaller
car.eqShorter: During a whole second the speed can change, so Δx/Δt only gives the average. Try a shorter Δt:
car.eqDerivative: The shorter Δt is, the closer we get to the speedometer. When Δt is so tiny it's almost zero, mathematicians call the result a derivative:
car.eqTangent: On the graphs, that's how steep the orange line is.
car.chartDistance: Distance from the start (m) as time passes
car.noteReady: Press the gas pedal to draw the graphs.
car.noteLive: The orange line touches each graph right now. On the distance graph its steepness is the speed; on the speed graph it's the acceleration. Touch a graph to stop time and look back.
car.noteScrub: Drag along a graph to look at any moment. The yellow car shows where you were.
car.sceneLabel: A car on a straight road, {x} m from the start, going {v} m/s.
car.whatText: Speed tells you how many metres the car covers each second: v = Δx/Δt. Acceleration tells you how much faster it gets each second: a = Δv/Δt. The pedals set the acceleration, not the speed. That's why the car keeps its speed when you let go: on a road with no friction, nothing slows it down.
car.shortcutsText: ↑: gas · ↓: brake (hold to press harder) · Space: pause · R: reset · 1/2/3: challenge · + / −: speed
